extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, observers and Royal Society readers (astronomers, experimentalists, anatomists) in late 17th century
extracted.subtask_description: Reports and methodological guidance for making and computing astronomical, biological, and physical observations (e.g., planetary transits, animal rearing, dissections, material measurements) with stepwise procedures and quantitative calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule for computing Mercury conjunction times after 33 years
rubrics_metrics.description: After 33 years Mercury passes over the sun 14' 2" more northerly; and the moment of the conjunction is had by subtracting from the time of the former, 3d. 0h. 23m. if it be the 3d year after bissextile; otherwise subtract 2d. 0h. 23m. only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use addition only to continue calculus for all conjunctions; from these adjustments one obtains moments of conjunctions and distances of the planet from sun's centre, then durations from a table of half-durations per minute of distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer observed epochs over purely calculated epochs
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the epocha, these are with more safety had from the industry of observers than by the subtilest calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose observed transit times (when available) as base cases for subsequent computations (the author used his full observation of the 1677 transit at St. Helena as the first case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute transit durations by adding/subtracting half-duration table values
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables of the half durations of these eclipses for each minute of distance seen from the sun's centre; which added to, and subtracted from, the moment of conjunction exhibit the beginning and end of the whole phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate the minute-distance from the sun's centre, read the corresponding semi-duration from the table, then add/subtract that interval to the computed conjunction moment to obtain ingress and egress times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit parallaxes in general Mercury calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: I have designedly omitted the parallaxes, as very inconsiderable, and which, being different in different places, could not be applied in a more general calculation; and because their quantity has not hitherto been determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a general table valid across places, neglect parallax for Mercury; apply parallax only when local correction is required or when more precise values are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect Mercury's diameter for most duration calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: I had also as little regard to Mercury's diameter, because, being extremely small, he seems to adhere for a very few minutes to the limb; ... therefore 31 minutes are spent, while the whole planet directly pervades the sun's limb; but, passing obliquely, he continues on it a little longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Mercury's diameter as negligible for broad duration tables; consider it only where limb-adhesion minutes materially affect measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Venus transits to determine solar distance by parallax
rubrics_metrics.description: By observing the ingress of Venus into, and egress from, the sun, the space of time between the moments of the internal contacts may be obtained to a second of time ... and thereby determine the distance of the sun from the earth with greatest certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure internal contact times at different places with high time resolution; use differences (parallax) to infer solar distance. The timing precision recommended is to a second using an ordinary telescope and a clock accurate for ~6–8 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for Venus's diameter and local parallaxes with place-specific calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: As the diameter of Venus is pretty large, and the parallaxes may cause a considerable difference as to the time, there must necessarily be a peculiar calculation for each place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on a single general table for Venus transits; compute ingress/egress durations and parallax corrections tailored to each observing location, accounting for Venus's larger apparent diameter (~1' 18" or 1' 12").

rubrics_metrics.name: Predict Venus transit intervals using orbital period relations
rubrics_metrics.description: From the elements (node longitude, distances, inclinations, motions in sidereal years over revolutions) make a calculus according to method explained in Mercury: after 8 years subtract 2d. 10h. 52m. and planet proceeds 24' 41" more southerly; after 235 years add 2d. 10h. 9m. (or add 3d.10h.9m. if preceding year bissextile) etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply specified day/hour minute adjustments depending on the cycle (8, 235, 243 years) and leap-year status to predict future transits and their displacement in latitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for dressing buck and doe skins (Indian method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pelt taken off, stretched by lines on a rack; brains taken out and dried on moss or grass; soak skins in pond/hole of water; scrape off hair with an old knife fixed in a cleft-stick while wet; put skins into kettle with proportion of dried brains warmed to lather and scour; wring/twist until no wet drop; stretch on a rack and as skin dries rub with a dull hatchet or smoothed stone to force out water and grease until perfectly dry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence of steps and small-tools specified; one woman can dress 8–10 skins in a day; men typically do not perform dressing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol for rearing and observing frog spawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect frog-spawn, keep in a gallipot of water changed every day or two, placed in a window with some sun; observe morphological stages: round black globule within clear liquor (day 1), progressive stages (days 2–4), hatching begins ~day 6, tail movements and rudiments of fore legs by ~14 days, mouths and faeces visible ~3 weeks, eyes discernible and surfacing behavior by ~1 month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record daily morphological changes, test responsiveness by pricking with a needle (contraction indicating viability), note buoyancy and specific gravity behavior of egg masses, and document timings for developmental stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated weighing protocol to assess tortoise seasonal weight change
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh tortoise before it withdraws to winter retreat and again upon reappearance in spring; repeat over series of years to compare weights at retreat and reappearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document exact dates and weights; use consistent weighing method to quantify weight loss or gain across hibernation cycles (examples show differences of ounces/drams across years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate gold-layer thickness and constituent particle size via gilt wire and specific gravities
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain manufacturing data (mass of silver ingots, ounces of gold used, weight per yard of fine wire), compute length covered per grain of gold, use specific gravities of silver and gold to deduce diameter and thickness of gold layer; infer number of atoms by dividing volumes accordingly (example gives gold thickness not to exceed ~1/100th of an inch fraction and huge atom counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine empirical workshop data (wire-drawers' reports) with measured specific gravities and basic geometry to estimate layer thickness; consider that extreme ductility and even texture imply many atoms may overlap even in very thin films.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmortem indicators of a diseased spleen
rubrics_metrics.description: A diseased spleen may be swollen and enlarged (dimensions and weight given), putrid in state with offensive smell, tender and friable like clotted blood, yet red internally and externally and without abscess or purulency; contrasts with scirrhous dark tumours commonly found in other cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record size, weight, texture, smell, color, presence/absence of abscesses or scirrhous tumors; consider patient history (sedentary life, menstrual issues) when reflecting on causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical description and functions of the periosteum
rubrics_metrics.description: Periosteum consists of two sorts of fibres (one from dura mater next to bone, one from tendons of muscles); uses: to cover bones, convey spirits into them for their sense, assist in nutrition (fibres inserted into bone), limit growth, keep some bones conjoined, join bones and cartilages, fasten heads and tendons to bones, and make bones sensible for directing remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing bone anatomy or performing dissections, identify the periosteum's two-fibre constitution and the multiple mechanical and nutritive roles ascribed; note fibres inserted into bone and pores/cavities for blood-vessels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model of bone structure and nutrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Bones initially gelatinous then cartilaginous, later hard and solid formed of terrestrial and saline particles united into strings and plates with two sorts of pores (those through plates and those between plates for medullary oil); cavities and fasciculi described; arteries enter and veins exit for nourishment; nutritive particles originate from chyle, elaborated in the blood and separated by glands on sides of arteries, then carried into small nervous pipes where spirits move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this structural model when interpreting bone growth and nutrition: describe plates, pores, cavities, vascular ingress/egress, and glandular separation of nutritive particles as steps in accretion and maintenance of bone substance.
